messages.author: f3e8911d01fbf32d
messages.subject: Image reproducibility deteriorates after processing.
parts:
Hi Cardinal users,

I deposited a standard with series dilutions onto a MALDI plate with two replicates (row 1 and row 2), and then I performed MALDI imaging analysis of the two rows together. 

Before preprocessing, I have checked the reproducibility of the result:

MALDI2_mix15 <- readMSIData(path, resolution = 10, units = "ppm", attach.only = T)
image(MALDI2_mix15, mz = 1034.564, smooth.image = "gaussian", plusminus = 0.001, contrast.enhance = "histogram", colorscale = magma)

Below is the MALDI image. The reproducibility is very good between the two replicates (row 1 and row 2)


While after Processing, the ion intensities of standards in row 1 were nearly undetectable. I don't know what was the problem. My Cardinal version is 2.2.6.

MALDI2 <- 
  MALDI2_mix15 %>%
  normalize(method = "tic") %>%
  peakPick(method = "mad") %>%
  peakAlign(tolerance = 10, units = "ppm") %>%
  process(BPPARAM=SerialParam())
 
mage(MALDI2_mix15, mz = 1034.564, smooth.image = "gaussian", plusminus = 0.001, contrast.enhance = "histogram", colorscale = magma) 



Could someone spot what the problem could be? Thanks a lot.


Hu

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Image reproducibility deteriorates after processing.
parts:
A couple possible things I can think of...

1. The normalization may be affecting the image, depending on the distribution of the rest of the ions in the spectra.

If the data is small enough that the normalized profile spectra can fit in memory, you could try checking the image after normalization only.

2. At 1034.56, a tolerance of 10 ppm is roughly 0.01 m/z, which is wider than the 0.001 m/z specified in the image.

Doing peakAlign() performs an implicit binning of any peaks detected within that tolerance, so it may be capturing a nearby adjacent peak for the lower row but not the top row.

3. Likely related to either (1) or (2) above, notice that the intensity scale is much different after the processing.

The ion intensities in the first row may still be detected, but much lower after some combination of the possible issues caused by (1) and (2).

I would check the image trying different combinations of no normalization and/or adjusting the tolerance to peakAlign(). I would also try widening the 'plusminus' in the original image and seeing if that leads to an image similar to the post-processing image.

-Kylie
